questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a correctly formed modal verb?
questions.explanation: A modal takes the base verb directly, with no -s on the modal and no "to": "You must wear" is the only correct form. "cans" and "musts" wrongly add -s, and "should to" wrongly adds "to".
"Don't" + base verb forbids something: don't phone in class. "should" gives advice (a good idea you can refuse), "might" says something is possible, and "can" expresses ability.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses "should" to give advice?

options.text: You should to eat more vegetables.

questions.explanation: "Should" takes the base verb with no "to" and no -ing: you should eat more vegetables. Only "ought" keeps a "to" (you ought to eat), and "should" never takes -s.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expresses an obligation in the past?

options.text: I must clean my room yesterday.
I had to clean my room yesterday.
I will have to clean my room yesterday.
I have to clean my room yesterday.

questions.explanation: Obligation in the past is "had to" + base verb: I had to clean my room yesterday. "must" has no past form, "have to" is the present and "will have to" is the future, which clashes with "yesterday".

questions.prompt: "Perhaps it will rain tomorrow." Which sentence has the same meaning?
questions.explanation: "Might" + base verb means "perhaps", so it replaces perhaps + will: it might rain tomorrow. A modal never takes -s ("mights" is wrong), "can't" says it is impossible, and "has to" expresses an obligation, not a possibility.
